:::{#def-link-function}
#### Link function

Let $\mu(\vx) \eqdef \E{Y|\vX=\vx}$ be the conditional mean of the outcome.
A **link function** is a monotone, differentiable function $g(\cdot)$
that relates the mean to the linear predictor (@def-linear-predictor):

$$
g\paren{\mu(\vx)} \eqdef \eta(\vx)
$$

[@dobson4e, Chapter 3; @dunn2018generalized, Chapter 5].
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-inverse-link}
#### Inverse link

When $g$ is strictly monotone on the range of possible means,
it has an inverse,
the **inverse link** $g^{-1}(\cdot)$,
which maps the linear predictor back to the mean:

$$
\mu(\vx) = g^{-1}\paren{\eta(\vx)}
$$
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-link-function}
#### Logit and log links

Take $\eta = 1.2$ from @exm-linear-predictor.
With the logit link $g(\mu) = \logit(\mu) = \logf{\frac{\mu}{1-\mu}}$,
the inverse link is $g^{-1}(\eta) = \expit(\eta) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-\eta}}$, so:

$$
\ba
\mu
&= \expit(1.2)
&& \text{(apply the inverse link)}
\\ &= \frac{1}{1 + e^{-1.2}}
&& \text{(definition of } \expit\text{)}
\\ &\approx \frac{1}{1 + 0.3012}
&& \text{(evaluate } e^{-1.2}\text{)}
\\ &= \frac{1}{1.3012}
&& \text{(add)}
\\ &\approx 0.7685
&& \text{(divide)}
\ea
$$

Applying the link to this mean recovers the linear predictor:

$$
\ba
\frac{\mu}{1-\mu}
&= \frac{1/(1 + e^{-1.2})}{e^{-1.2}/(1 + e^{-1.2})}
&& \text{(since } 1 - \mu = e^{-1.2}/(1 + e^{-1.2})\text{)}
\\ &= \frac{1}{e^{-1.2}}
&& \text{(cancel } 1 + e^{-1.2}\text{)}
\\ &= e^{1.2}
&& \text{(reciprocal of an exponential)}
\\ \logit(\mu)
&= \logf{e^{1.2}}
&& \text{(take logs)}
\\ &= 1.2
&& \text{(log inverts exp)}
\ea
$$

With the log link $g(\mu) = \logf{\mu}$ instead,
the inverse link is $g^{-1}(\eta) = \expf{\eta}$,
so the same linear predictor gives $\mu = e^{1.2} \approx 3.320$.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-not-link-function}
#### A function that is not a link function

For a Gaussian outcome, whose mean can be any real number,
$g(\mu) = \mu^2$ is not a valid link function,
because it is not monotone on $(-\infty, \infty)$.
Both $\mu = -1$ and $\mu = 1$ give $g(\mu) = 1$,
so a linear predictor $\eta(\vx) = 1$ does not determine the mean,
and $g$ has no inverse link.
:::
